body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Saturday, October 3, and the day's top story is a hard-fought night for local fire crews, who spent their Friday evening in defensive mode at a multi-structure fire near Pond Road and Minner Avenue after power lines came down. The other headline is the heat: expect a high near 100 degrees today, with no active weather alerts for Kern County and no fires reported in the region.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call came at 9:27 p.m., when fire crews were sent to a report of a house fire near Pond Road and Minner Avenue. A battalion chief arriving on scene found multiple structures involved and power lines down across the property, and crews shifted into a defensive mode, with water tenders shuttling in to supply the fight. Before they could work the property, crews asked the utility to cut the downed lines. Later in the evening, they reported the resident had been contacted and gave a verbal all clear for the property. No injuries were reported in the initial dispatch.

Earlier in the evening, at 11:29 p.m., deputies were sent to a mobile home park after a resident who uses a wheelchair reported that two men took $200 in cash at gunpoint roughly fifteen minutes earlier and then ran off on foot. Around 12:32 a.m., officers were sent to an apartment on the 400 block of White Lane after a resident who lives alone reported that someone had come in through her front door, that she heard an item fall inside her kitchen, and that she was hiding in her closet. Units checked the apartments around the call and did not find anyone.

In the early morning hours, at 2:20 a.m., a semi pulling a dry van trailer and a day cab truck pulling a trash trailer were involved in a crash on southbound Interstate 5 north of Gorman. One truck was reported to have right-side damage, and the other driver pulled over on the wide shoulder just south of Gorman. Then, at 2:57 a.m., a ShotSpotter activation reported eight rounds fired in the 1700 block of Niles Street, and officers were sent to check the area.

The rest of the log was a mix of medical aids, alarms and traffic checks. At 9:13 p.m., deputies were sent to a store on 20 Mule Team Road in Boron, where a man had facial injuries and could not stand; crews started medical aid. At 9:18 p.m., callers reported people in a white SUV inhaling from balloons in an apartment complex parking lot on the 2300 block of South K Street. At 9:35 p.m., a woman on Plymouth Avenue reported hiding from people who live at a home and said a man in his 20s was in the back alley. At 9:58 p.m., a car was reported stolen minutes earlier from the 2300 block of Niles Street, and the description went out to units. And at 10:11 p.m., a caller reported a white SUV running recklessly on westbound Highway 58 near Oswell Street.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 100 degrees today and a low around 71 tonight. It's currently 77 degrees at Meadows Field, which is a comfortable start before the heat settles in this afternoon. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality and fire information were not available at the time of this report. If you're headed out, plan around the heat — morning is the better window for yard work, errands, or anything that keeps you in the sun.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield police are searching for a man who allegedly broke into Howard's Mini Mart through the roof.** The department is asking the public for help identifying the suspect, who is accused of getting into the business from above rather than through a door or window. Anyone with information should reach out to BPD directly.

**According to 23ABC, the victims of a deadly helicopter crash off Catalina Island have been identified.** REACH Air Medical Services says pilot Steven "Steve" Robinson and flight nurse Jessica deVries died after a medical helicopter crashed in the Catalina waters shortly after takeoff on September 30. The helicopter was transporting a patient, identified as Catalina Hernandez, to the mainland for emergency care; her body was recovered after she had gone missing. Another flight nurse on board, Brad Sparks, continues his recovery, and Hernandez's son, who was with her during the flight, survived the crash. "This tragedy has touched every corner of our organization," said Pacific Region President Sean Russell.

**KGET 17 tells us a man faces life in prison after killing his wife, in a case where loved ones remembered the victim with the words, "They were all here every day."** The conviction closes a chapter for a family that had been present and visible in the victim's life, and the sentence now rests with the court.

**KGET 17 also reports that two Garces football stars are ineligible for Friday's game, leaving the status of the team's wins up in the air.** The eligibility question puts the program's season record under scrutiny while the matter is resolved — a story worth watching for Garces families and anyone following local high school football.

**23ABC reports that the Bakersfield Condors open their 2026-27 AHL season this weekend in Henderson, Nevada, with captain Seth Griffith back for his seventh season in Condorstown.** Griffith has served as captain, helped develop younger players and watched teammates move up to the Edmonton Oilers — but he still hasn't won a Calder Cup. "I haven't won a Calder Cup," Griffith said. "You see the Marlies do it last year and you see how much fun they had celebrating and really becoming a team. I think that's what it's all about." He said the older players try to instill daily work ethic and professional habits so that when younger players get their chance in Edmonton, "it's not out of the blue for them." The Condors used nearly 40 players last season, and Griffith said creating a role for everyone matters: "We need every man on board." The team begins the year with four straight road games.

**23ABC also reports that a sexual assault case at Cornell University is drawing national attention to a question at the heart of criminal law: when does intoxication make it legally impossible to consent?** Jane Doe, a former Cornell student, says she was drugged and sexually assaulted by fraternity members in 2024; the men accused deny wrongdoing, no criminal charges have been filed, and the case is back under criminal review, with New York Attorney General Letitia James appointed special prosecutor. 23ABC spoke with Jared Thompson, a criminal law attorney and specialist with the State Bar, about how California would handle a similar case. Under California law, Thompson said, "The prosecution has to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the person was so intoxicated that they didn't understand the nature of the act… they didn't understand the consequences." The law also requires proof the accused knew — or reasonably should have known — that the other party could not consent, and California does not require a survivor to have been unconscious or physically unable to speak.

**KGET 17 reports that prosecutor Pedro Naveiras is making public safety the centerpiece of his bid for Bakersfield's third ward.** Naveiras is leaning into his courtroom experience as the core of his campaign message to voters in that ward.

## Something good

A good note for Condors fans: Seth Griffith is back for a seventh season in Bakersfield, still chasing the Calder Cup. His continued commitment to the local team gives the city another season of professional hockey to look forward to — and a captain who clearly cares about the players coming up behind him. Heading into a season that starts with four road games, that kind of steady leadership is worth a smile.

## Coming up this week

Public meetings fill the calendar starting today. A Special Youth Commission meets Saturday, October 3, at 9 a.m. The Youth Commission holds its regular meeting Monday, October 5, at 4:30 p.m. Then Wednesday, October 7, is the busiest day: the Police Civil Service Commission meets at 8:30 a.m., City Council Meeting 330 convenes at 3:30 p.m., and City Council Meeting 515 follows at 5:15 p.m. Later in the week, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets Thursday, October 8, at noon, and the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets Friday, October 9, at noon.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. "Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein" screens Monday, October 5. The NB RIDAZ "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off" tour comes through Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. "United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night." takes the stage Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour arrives Saturday, October 17. Also worth noting: the Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026-2027 is on sale now for anyone who wants the whole series. Have a safe, cool Saturday, Bakersfield.

top.title: BPD: Search for man who allegedly broke into Howard’s Mini Mart through the roof
